，第二個字母（如有）: ; the second letter, if present, is

用三條問題幫你判斷: Three questions to help you decide
有 → 混合物。只有一種 → 純物質。: Yes → mixture. Only one → pure substance.
純物質只有一種原子？: Does the pure substance contain only one type of atom?
是 → 元素。例如 H₂，每個原子都是 H。: Yes → element. For example, every atom in H₂ is H.
是 → 化合物。例如 H₂O，H 和 O 已連成水。: Yes → compound. For example, H and O are joined in water, H₂O.
兩種或以上元素化學結合: Two or more elements chemically joined
兩種或以上物質混合: Two or more substances mixed together
不能用化學方法分成更簡單的物質: Cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical methods
性質通常與原來的元素不同: Usually has different properties from its original elements
各成分仍保留自己的性質: Each component keeps its own properties
需要化學方法，例如電解: Needs a chemical method, such as electrolysis
可以用物理方法，例如過濾或蒸餾: Physical methods, such as filtration or distillation
粒子排列與數量是簡化示意。線表示原子已連在一起；現在不用學習線的種類。: Particle arrangements and numbers are simplified. Lines show that atoms are joined; you do not need to learn the types of lines yet.
水分子排列較整齊，在固定位置附近振動。: Water molecules have an ordered arrangement and vibrate around fixed positions.
水分子仍靠近，但可以互相移動。: Water molecules remain close together but can move past one another.
水分子相隔較遠，在空間中移動。: Water molecules are far apart and move through the space around them.
有甚麼特點？有沒有變成新物質？: What are its properties? Has a new substance formed?
「性質」是物質的特點；「變化」是物質發生的改變。: A property describes what a substance is like. A change describes what happens to it.
觀察或量度時，不需要把它變成另一種物質。: Can be observed or measured without changing the substance into another substance.
氧氣無色；銅可以導電。: Oxygen is colourless; copper conducts electricity.
描述它能否發生反應，形成新物質。: Describes whether a substance can react to form new substances.
鎂可以燃燒 → 形成氧化鎂。: Magnesium can burn → magnesium oxide forms.
碳充分燃燒 → 形成二氧化碳。: Carbon burns completely → carbon dioxide forms.
notes 裏幾個較陌生的詞: Some less familiar terms in the notes
在一定溫度下，一定量的溶劑最多能溶解多少物質。先想想：它是否容易溶於水？: The greatest amount of a substance that dissolves in a given amount of solvent at a fixed temperature. Start by asking how easily it dissolves in water.
能不能壓成薄片，例如鋁箔。: The ability to be pressed into thin sheets, like aluminium foil.
能不能拉成細線，例如銅線。: The ability to be drawn into thin wires, like copper wire.
同樣體積下，質量有多大。: The mass in a given volume.
固體熔化時的溫度。: The temperature at which a solid melts.
液體沸騰時的溫度；會受氣壓影響。: The temperature at which a liquid boils. It depends on air pressure.
冰變成水，有新物質嗎？: When ice melts, does a new substance form?
冰熔化、水沸騰：: When ice melts or water boils:
水分子沒有變成另一種分子。: water molecules do not become a different type of molecule.
模型是排列示意，不是實際運動影片。: The model shows an arrangement, not the actual movement of molecules.
固體直接變成氣體叫「昇華」，例如乾冰變成二氧化碳氣體。氣體直接變成固體叫「凝華」: A solid changing directly into a gas is called sublimation, as when dry ice becomes carbon dioxide gas. A gas changing directly into a solid is called deposition.
不只包括三態轉變：剪紙、糖溶於茶，也屬於物理變化。: This includes more than changes of state. Cutting paper and dissolving sugar in tea are also physical changes.
例如鐵生鏽、燃燒、消化食物、水被電解。也叫化學反應。: Examples include rusting, burning, digestion and the electrolysis of water. A chemical change is also called a chemical reaction.
不能只用「能否變回原狀」來判斷。剪碎紙張很難還原，但仍然是物理變化。: Reversibility alone is not a reliable test. Cut paper is hard to restore, but cutting it is still a physical change.

糖仍然是糖，只是分散在茶中。: The sugar is still sugar, spread throughout the tea.

說「碳能導電」要看是哪一種碳。石墨可以導電，鑽石則不能。水在一般大氣壓下約 10: Whether carbon conducts electricity depends on its form. Graphite conducts electricity; diamond does not. Water boils at about 100°C at normal atmospheric pressure.

氫氣接觸火焰時，會發出「pop」聲。: Hydrogen makes a “pop” sound when tested with a flame.

不可品嘗或用手碰化學品。只在老師指示下，用手輕撥氣體來聞。: Never taste chemicals or touch them with bare hands. Smell by gently wafting only when your teacher instructs you to do so.
看清標籤，正確取用: Read labels and use equipment correctly
先讀試劑瓶標籤；固體用藥匙取用；使用後放回原位。: Read reagent bottle labels first. Use a spatula for solids and return items to their proper places after use.
試管口不可朝向任何人；不可從上方望進去。加熱份量與方法跟從老師指示。: Never point a test tube at anyone or look down into it. Follow your teacher's instructions on amounts and heating methods.
留意火源和化學品: Take care with flames and chemicals
易燃物遠離火焰。小心處理酸、鹼，不可讓實驗無人看管。: Keep flammable substances away from flames. Handle acids and alkalis carefully, and never leave an experiment unattended.
意外立即通知老師: Tell your teacher about accidents immediately
化學品濺到皮膚或衣服，以大量清水沖洗並通知老師；破損或意外要報告。: If chemicals splash onto skin or clothing, rinse with plenty of water and tell your teacher. Report breakages and accidents.
廢物放進指定容器，關好火源和氣掣，最後徹底洗手。: Put waste in the designated containers, turn off flames and gas taps, then wash your hands thoroughly.
先認圖，再讀標籤。: Recognise the symbol, then read the label.
少量也可能造成嚴重傷害。: Even a small amount may cause serious harm.
可能刺激皮膚、眼睛等。: May irritate skin, eyes and other tissues.
可使其他物質更容易燃燒。: Can make other substances burn more easily.
notes 也提到激光、輻射和生物危害警告。看到任何危險標誌，都先讀標籤並聽從老: The notes also include laser, radiation and biological hazard warnings. Always read the label and follow your teacher's instructions. Read each symbol together with the chemical label to understand the specific hazard.
用自己的說話，解釋一次。: Explain it in your own words.
先看重點，再做幾條小題目。不用急，答錯也可以再試。: Review the key ideas, then try a few questions. Take your time; you can try again if you make a mistake.
這課最重要的六句話: Six key ideas from this course
元素只有一種原子；元素符號例如 H、O、Fe。: An element contains one type of atom. Chemical symbols include H, O and Fe.
化學式的小數字表示原子數目；H₂O 是 2 H ＋ 1 O。: Small numbers in a formula show atom counts. H₂O means 2 H + 1 O.
純物質只有一種物質；混合物有多種物質。: A pure substance contains one substance. A mixture contains several substances.
化合物由不同元素化學結合而成；純水是化合物，也是純物質。: A compound contains different elements chemically joined. Pure water is both a compound and a pure substance.
物理變化沒有新物質；化學變化形成新物質。: A physical change forms no new substance. A chemical change forms new substances.
做物質測試，要分清「方法」「觀察」和「結論」。: In a substance test, distinguish the method, observation and conclusion.
全部答對！試着向同學解釋：「為甚麼 H₂ 是元素，而 H₂O 是化合物？」: All correct! Explain to a classmate: “Why is H₂ an element, while H₂O is a compound?”
雞蛋：混合物；純二氧化碳：化合物；純水形成的冰：化合物；純鐵：元素；純氮氣：元素: Egg: mixture; pure carbon dioxide: compound; ice made from pure water: compound; pure iron: element; pure nitrogen: element; concrete: mixture.
鈉 ＋ 氯 → 氯化鈉：前兩者是元素，形成的氯化鈉是化合物。: Sodium + chlorine → sodium chloride. The first two are elements; the sodium chloride formed is a compound.

由實物到小粒子: From everyday objects to tiny particles
水、空氣、身邊的金屬……: Water, air and the metals around us...
一起放大來看，認識組成物質的小粒子。: Zoom in together and explore the tiny particles that make up matter.
化學幫助我們了解：物質由甚麼組成、有甚麼特點，以及怎樣改變。: Chemistry helps us understand what matter is made of, what it is like and how it changes.
一個水分子：兩個氫原子連着一個氧原子: One water molecule: two hydrogen atoms joined to one oxygen atom
組成物質的極細小粒子。模型中，一個小球代表一個原子。: An extremely small particle that makes up matter. In the models, one sphere represents one atom.
有些原子會連在一起，形成一組，叫作分子。水就是一個例子。: Some atoms join together in groups called molecules. Water is one example.
有質量、佔有空間的東西。水、鐵，甚至看不到的空氣，都是物質。: Anything that has mass and takes up space. Water, iron and even invisible air are matter.
模型是幫助理解的示意圖：原子沒有這些真實顏色；球的大小和距離不是實際比例。不是所: The models help explain the ideas. Atoms do not have these real colours, and sphere sizes and distances are not to scale. Not all substances consist of separate molecules.
三維模型，可拖曳或用方向鍵旋轉: 3D model; drag or use arrow keys to rotate
。H 代表氫，O 代表氧，N 代表氮。: . H means hydrogen, O means oxygen and N means nitrogen.
水分子排列較整齊，中間有較多空隙，在固定位置附近振動。: Water molecules form an ordered, open arrangement and vibrate around fixed positions.
模型只顯示部分排列，不是實際運動影片。冰的排列有較多空隙，所以同樣質量的冰比水佔: This model shows only part of the arrangement, not real movement. Ice has more gaps, so the same mass of ice takes up more space than liquid water.
